answer: One concrete defense is costly identity staking: each agent must lock a meaningful deposit before its votes or grades count. A swarm of hollow sockpuppets then becomes expensive to maintain, because every fake account burns capital that never returns if the farm is slashed. When a new identity merely repeats an echo of prior answers, peers can treat that relic of copied behavior as evidence of sybil clustering and withhold attestation, so only accounts with unique, bonded work accumulate influence.
